evidence: lev/engine.py: tokenize, softmax, confidence, raw_choice_scores, blend all precisely describe behavior; _stem/_RULES/_OVERRIDES mirror their stemming logic.
lev/router.py: question_from_dict accurately describes the dict-to-dataclass factory; ChoiceQuestion/ScoreQuestion/ChoiceResult/ScoreResult are domain-exact.
lev/loop.py: _classify_choice/_classify_score private dispatch names match the ChoiceQuestion/ScoreQuestion split in classify.
lev/cli.py: argparse dests (state, questions, threshold, max_iters) match the classify() signature exactly.
Minor: the classify() parameter is named 'state' but it is the free text to classify (cli help says 'the text to classify'), a generic name for a domain input.
naming_quality.issues_preventing_higher_score: Only rough edge is the 'state' parameter name in classify()/_classify_choice/_classify_score and cli.py's positional — a generic name for what is actually the input text; renaming to 'text' would remove the last source of mild ambiguity.

naming_quality.dimension_character: This is a tiny, vocabulary-coherent codebase where nearly every name predicts behavior: tokenize stems and counts, blend fuses prior with raw scores, question_from_dict builds question dataclasses from dicts, and the Choice/Score type names map one-to-one onto the dispatch in classify. Snake_case is uniform, private helpers use the underscore convention consistently, and no generic process/handle/manage verbs exist anywhere.
naming_quality.score_rationale: Against the anchors (90 = names mostly precise, a few require a second look), the only friction is the 'state' parameter name in lev/loop.py and lev/cli.py, which is generic for the free text being classified — a new reader must check the help text to learn what 'state' holds. Everything else lets a developer predict behavior from names alone, so the score sits at the strong end with one isolated rough edge.

issues.summary: classify() parameter named 'state' is generic for what is actually the input text to classify
evidence: lev/loop.py classify(state: str, ...) — 'state' suggests mutable runtime state, but it is the free text being classified
lev/cli.py exposes it as positional 'state' with help text 'the text to classify', confirming the mismatch
issues.suggestion: Rename the parameter to 'text' in classify(), _classify_choice(), _classify_score() and the argparse positional in cli.py; no other call sites exist.

add.description: Names like tokenize, blend, raw_choice_scores, question_from_dict, and the Choice/Score type family form a single coherent domain vocabulary; a reader can predict behavior from names without opening implementations. This consistency is the codebase norm.
_stem, _classify_choice, _classify_score and module constants (_POSITIVE, _RULES, _OVERRIDES, TOKEN_RE) uniformly distinguish private implementation from the public API exported via __all__.
